#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Does the project chat's model answer a how-to question from the app guide?

Each question in guide_questions.json belongs to one page of docs/guide. A run
sends the question as a chat's first message and passes when the model's reply
tells the person what the question's "answer" says, in the judge's reading. The
run's line also says whether the model read the page's skill
(skills/guide-<area>/SKILL.md) on the way.

The request is the recorded "advice-infill" point with the person's sentence
replaced, so the prompt, the tools and the workspace are the app's, and a
skill_read of a guide is answered with the skill as checked in. Everything
else is run_prompt_tests.py: the same options, backends and judge.

    tests/project_prompt/run_guide_tests.py --backend claude-cli --judge claude-cli --runs 1
    tests/project_prompt/run_guide_tests.py --area print-settings --no-guide ...

--area keeps the questions of one page. --no-guide takes every guide off the
list skill_read carries, which is the app before the guide: the gap between
the two runs is what the guide does.
"""
import copy
import json
import pathlib
import sys

import run_prompt_tests as runner

HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
SKILLS = HERE / "../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/skills"
QUESTIONS = json.loads((HERE / "guide_questions.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
POINT = "advice-infill"


def skill_text(area):
    """The text skill_read returns: the skill file after its front matter."""
    return (SKILLS / f"guide-{area}" / "SKILL.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8").split("\n---\n", 1)[1].strip()


def add_case(area, entry, with_guide):
    skill = f"guide-{area}"

    class GuideQuestion(runner.Case):
        def check(self, step):
            if step.tool:
                return (runner.FAIL if step.changes() else runner.CONTINUE), str(step)
            read = any("skill_read" in line and skill in line for line in self.log)
            yes, why = self.judged(step, f"Does the assistant's last message tell the person {entry['answer']}?")
            tag = "[read the guide] " if read else "[did not read the guide] "
            return (runner.PASS, tag + str(step)) if yes else (runner.FAIL, tag + "WRONG OR MISSING PLACE: " + why)

    GuideQuestion.name = f"guide-{area}-{entry['id']}"
    GuideQuestion.__doc__ = entry["question"]
    point = copy.deepcopy(runner.REQUESTS[POINT])
    point["body"]["input"][0]["content"][0]["text"] = entry["question"]
    if with_guide:
        answer = copy.deepcopy(next(a for a in point["answers"] if a["tool"] == "skill_read"))
        output = json.loads(answer["output"])
        output["result"] = {"name": skill, "text": skill_text(area)}
        answer["arguments"] = {"name": skill}
        answer["output"] = json.dumps(output, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"))
        point["answers"].append(answer)
    runner.REQUESTS[GuideQuestion.name] = point
    runner.CASES[GuideQuestion.name] = GuideQuestion
    return GuideQuestion.name


def take(flag, has_value):
    """Removes this script's own option from the command line and returns it."""
    if flag not in sys.argv:
        return None
    at = sys.argv.index(flag)
    value = sys.argv[at + 1] if has_value else True
    del sys.argv[at:at + (2 if has_value else 1)]
    return value


def main():
    area = take("--area", True)
    with_guide = not take("--no-guide", False)
    if area is not None and area not in QUESTIONS:
        sys.exit(f"no questions for {area}: guide_questions.json has {', '.join(sorted(QUESTIONS))}")
    if not with_guide:
        tool = next(tool for tool in runner.TOOLS if tool.get("name") == "skill_read")
        tool["description"] = "\n".join(line for line in tool["description"].split("\n") if not line.startswith("- guide-"))
    names = [add_case(each, entry, with_guide)
             for each in sorted(QUESTIONS) if area in (None, each) for entry in QUESTIONS[each]]
    if "--case" not in sys.argv:
        for name in names:
            sys.argv += ["--case", name]
    runner.main()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

## The app guide's questions (`run_guide_tests.py`)

The pages of `docs/guide` are also skills the model reads (`guide-<area>`,
built by `AgentUI/src/guide.ts`). `run_guide_tests.py` measures whether the
model answers a how-to question from them. It is not one of the cases above
and has no baseline: run it when a page, its skill's description or the
prompt's wording about skills changes.

```bash
tests/project_prompt/run_guide_tests.py --backend claude-cli --judge claude-cli
tests/project_prompt/run_guide_tests.py --area print-settings --no-guide --backend claude-cli --judge claude-cli
```

- `guide_questions.json` holds, per page, the questions and what a right
  answer tells the person. `guide.test.ts` fails when a page has fewer than
  three questions, so a new page brings its own.
- Each question is sent as a chat's first message: the recorded
  `advice-infill` request with the person's sentence replaced. A `skill_read`
  of a guide is answered with the skill as checked in, and the judge is asked
  whether the reply tells the person what the question's `answer` says. A run's
  line says whether the model read the guide on the way.
- `--no-guide` takes the guides off the list `skill_read` carries, which is
  the app before the guide. The gap between the two runs is what the guide
  does.
- `--area NAME` keeps one page's questions. Three runs a question unless
  `--runs` says otherwise; every other option is `run_prompt_tests.py`'s.
- The expected answers are written from the page, so a pass says the model
  read the page and relayed it, not that the page is right. The page is
  checked against the app by its own checks (`docs/guide/README.md`).

- **`design-guidelines.md`, "How a screen gets designed and checked", step 8:** "Check it in the running app. Take screenshots of the built screen along one real path". The "cold-reader check" section adds: use screenshots "from one coherent path"; give a fresh agent only the screenshots.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Checks the app guide against the running app and takes its pictures.

guide_checks.json names, for each page of docs/guide, the shell harness runs
that walk the screens the page describes. Each run drives the real app in a
data folder of its own, asserts what it finds (HARNESS CHECK lines) and writes
pictures of it. This script runs them, fails when a run fails, and copies the
pictures a page uses into docs/guide/pictures/<page>/, so a page's steps and
its pictures are both taken from the app as built.

    tests/shell/run_guide_checks.py                  every page
    tests/shell/run_guide_checks.py --area print-settings
    tests/shell/run_guide_checks.py --list           what would run; runs nothing

The harness is the newest one under build/ (the shell_integration_harness
target), or JUSPRIN_SHELL_HARNESS. A run opens the app's window on this
computer's screen: leave the screen unlocked and the window uncovered, and on
a Mac grant the harness Screen Recording once, or its pictures come out blank.
--keep DIR keeps every run's log and all the pictures it wrote.
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import pathlib
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time

HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = HERE.parent.parent
CHECKS = json.loads((HERE / "guide_checks.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
PICTURES = ROOT / "docs/guide/pictures"
HARNESS_NAMES = ("JusPrinShellHarness", "shell_integration_harness", "shell_integration_harness.exe")
TIME_LIMIT = 1000  # the harness gives up by itself at 900 s


def harness():
    named = os.environ.get("JUSPRIN_SHELL_HARNESS")
    if named:
        return pathlib.Path(named)
    built = [path for name in HARNESS_NAMES for path in (ROOT / "build").rglob(name) if path.is_file()]
    if not built:
        sys.exit("the shell harness is not built: build the shell_integration_harness target or set JUSPRIN_SHELL_HARNESS")
    return max(built, key=lambda path: path.stat().st_mtime)


def run(binary, entry, out, log):
    """One harness run. Returns whether it passed and the checks that failed."""
    args = [str(out) if arg == "{dir}" else arg for arg in entry["args"]]
    env = dict(os.environ, **{name: str(out) if value == "{dir}" else value for name, value in entry.get("env", {}).items()})
    try:
        done = subprocess.run([str(binary), *args], env=env, capture_output=True, text=True, errors="replace", timeout=TIME_LIMIT)
        text = done.stdout + done.stderr
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as late:
        text = f"{late.stdout or ''}{late.stderr or ''}\nHARNESS RESULT FAIL (no result after {TIME_LIMIT} s)"
    log.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
    failed = re.findall(r"HARNESS CHECK (\S+) FAIL", text) + re.findall(r"HARNESS ERROR (.+)", text)
    checks = len(re.findall(r"HARNESS CHECK \S+ PASS", text))
    return "HARNESS RESULT PASS" in text, failed, checks


def copy_pictures(area, entry, out):
    """Copies the run's pictures the page uses. Returns the names it could not."""
    missing = []
    for name, source in entry.get("pictures", {}).items():
        made = out / source
        if not made.is_file() or made.stat().st_size == 0:
            missing.append(f"{name} (the run wrote no {source})")
            continue
        target = PICTURES / area / name
        target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        # An unchanged picture is left alone, so a run that changes nothing changes no file.
        if not target.is_file() or target.read_bytes() != made.read_bytes():
            shutil.copyfile(made, target)
    return missing


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    parser.add_argument("--area", choices=sorted(CHECKS), help="check only this page")
    parser.add_argument("--list", action="store_true", help="print what would run and stop")
    parser.add_argument("--keep", metavar="DIR", help="keep each run's log and every picture it wrote here")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    areas = [args.area] if args.area else sorted(CHECKS)
    if args.list:
        for area in areas:
            for entry in CHECKS[area]:
                print(f"{area}: {' '.join(entry['args']) or '(default run)'} -> {', '.join(entry['covers'])}")
        return
    binary = harness()
    keep = pathlib.Path(args.keep) if args.keep else pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="jusprin-guide-"))
    print(f"harness {binary}\nlogs and pictures in {keep}")
    problems = 0
    for area in areas:
        for index, entry in enumerate(CHECKS[area], 1):
            label = " ".join(arg for arg in entry["args"] if arg != "{dir}") or "(default run)"
            out = keep / area / f"{index}-{label.strip('-() ').replace(' ', '-') or 'default'}"
            out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            started = time.time()
            passed, failed, checks = run(binary, entry, out, out / "harness.log")
            missing = copy_pictures(area, entry, out) if passed else []
            verdict = "pass" if passed and not missing else "FAIL"
            print(f"{area}: {label}: {verdict} ({checks} checks, {int(time.time() - started)} s) covers {', '.join(entry['covers'])}")
            for line in failed[:10]:
                print(f"    failed: {line}")
            for line in missing:
                print(f"    no picture: {line}")
            problems += verdict == "FAIL"
    print(f"{problems} of the runs failed" if problems else "every run passed")
    sys.exit(1 if problems else 0)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Checks the app guide (docs/guide) from end to end, and rebuilds what is
built from it. Run it after editing a page, and before a release.

     (tests/shell/run_guide_checks.py). Needs the shell_integration_harness
     and jusprin_web targets built from this checkout, and this computer's

     a page quotes is in the source, that every section has a run in step 1,
     that every picture is one step 1 took, and that every page has questions
     for step 3 (AgentUI's guide.test.ts).
  3. With --ask-ai: asks the model each page's questions and has a judge read
     the answers (tests/project_prompt/run_guide_tests.py), on the Claude

    scripts/check_guide.py
    scripts/check_guide.py --area print-settings --ask-ai
    scripts/check_guide.py --skip-app             steps 2 and 3 only
    scripts/check_guide.py --ask-ai -- --runs 1   options after -- go to step 3

Exits 0 when every step it ran passed.
"""
import argparse
import os
import pathlib
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys

ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
AGENT_UI = ROOT / "src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI"


def step(title, command, cwd=ROOT, env=None):
    print(f"\n== {title}\n   {' '.join(map(str, command))}", flush=True)
    return subprocess.run(command, cwd=cwd, env=env).returncode == 0


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Checks the app guide and rebuilds what is built from it.")
    parser.add_argument("--area", help="one page, by its file name without .md")
    parser.add_argument("--skip-app", action="store_true", help="do not run the app: no walk, no new pictures")
    parser.add_argument("--ask-ai", action="store_true", help="also ask the model each page's questions")
    parser.add_argument("rest", nargs="*", help="after --: options for the questions run")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    area = ["--area", args.area] if args.area else []
    npx = shutil.which("npx")
    if npx is None:
        sys.exit("npx is not on PATH: the page checks need node")

    results = {}
    if not args.skip_app:
        results["the app walk and pictures"] = step(
            "1/3 walking the pages in the app and taking their pictures",
            [sys.executable, ROOT / "tests/shell/run_guide_checks.py", *area])
    results["skills, labels, sections, pictures and questions"] = step(
        "2/3 rebuilding the skills AI reads and checking the pages",
        [npx, "vitest", "run", "src/guide.test.ts"], cwd=AGENT_UI,
        env=dict(os.environ, JUSPRIN_UPDATE_GUIDE_SKILLS="1"))
    if args.ask_ai:
        options = args.rest or ["--backend", "claude-cli", "--judge", "claude-cli"]
        # The questions run exits 2 when it has no baseline to compare with, which it never has.
        print("\n== 3/3 asking the model each page's questions", flush=True)
        asked = subprocess.run([sys.executable, ROOT / "tests/project_prompt/run_guide_tests.py", *area, "--must-pass", "1", *options],
                               cwd=ROOT)
        results["the model's answers"] = asked.returncode == 0

    print()
    for name, passed in results.items():
        print(f"{'pass' if passed else 'FAIL'}: {name}")
    sys.exit(0 if all(results.values()) else 1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# JusPrin guide

How to use JusPrin, one page per part of the app.

- [Seeing and changing print settings](print-settings.md)

## Writing a page

A page is read by people here and, in the app, by AI. Four things are made or checked from it, all by one command:

```bash
scripts/check_guide.py --ask-ai
```

1. **The app walk and the pictures.** `tests/shell/guide_checks.json` names, for each page, the runs of the app's test harness that walk the screens the page describes. Each run drives the app as built, checks what it finds, and writes pictures. `tests/shell/run_guide_checks.py` runs them and copies the pictures a page uses into `pictures/<page>/`. It needs the `shell_integration_harness` and `jusprin_web` targets built, and this computer's screen.
2. **The copy AI reads.** `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/guide.ts` builds a skill from the page, and it is committed with the page.
3. **The page's own checks**, in `guide.test.ts` beside it: every label in bold is still in the app's source, every section has a run in step 1, every picture is one step 1 took, and the page has questions for step 4.
4. **The answers AI gives** (`--ask-ai`). `tests/project_prompt/guide_questions.json` holds each page's questions and what a right answer says. `tests/project_prompt/run_guide_tests.py` asks the model and has a judge read the replies.

The rules for a page:

- Start it with `<!-- ai-description: … -->`: one line, at most 300 bytes, saying when AI should read it.
- Put words that are only for AI in `<!-- ai: … -->`. They are hidden on this site.
- Use bold only for words that are on screen, exactly as they are on screen.
- A picture goes on a line of its own, as `![what it shows](pictures/<page>/<name>.png)`, and comes from a run named in `guide_checks.json`. AI's copy leaves it out.
- Give each `##` section a run in `guide_checks.json`. If no harness run walks that screen yet, add one to the harness first.
- Add at least three questions for the page to `guide_questions.json`.
- AI's copy may hold at most 16 KiB. Split a page that grows past that.

one script doesn't do everything we discussed, right? Tell me your understanding about what should happen.

Right, it does not. The one command only checks a page that already exists and rebuilds what is derived from it. Here is what I understand should happen, and where the gaps are.

**What should happen, as I understand it**

1. **Someone changes a screen and forgets the guide.** Say a button is renamed from "All settings" to "Every setting". A check should fail on that change by itself and name the page and the label, with nobody having to remember to run anything.
2. **The page then gets fixed with almost no human work.** An agent rewrites the affected steps from the code, retakes the pictures from the running app, rebuilds the AI's copy, and re-asks the AI the page's questions. A person only reads the resulting diff.
3. **Someone adds a new screen or menu item.** A check should notice that no page mentions it.
4. **A release goes out.** The pictures are retaken on that build, the AI's copy ships inside the app, and the Help menu opens the guide as it was at that version.
5. **A person needs help.** They ask the AI, which reads the page and answers, and can point them to the page with its pictures. Or they open the guide from the Help menu.
6. **All seven areas of the app are covered,** not one.

**Where each of those stands**

| What should happen | Today |
|---|---|
| A check fails by itself when a label changes | The check exists, but nothing runs it automatically. No CI job runs the page tests, and a pull request into `jusprin-dev` runs no build or test jobs at all. |
| An agent rewrites the page from the code | Not built. I wrote the one page by hand, and there is no written procedure an agent could follow. |
| Pictures retaken by script | The script exists and is running now for the first time. No picture is in the page yet. It works on a Mac with the screen unlocked; Windows and Linux are untried. |
| AI's copy rebuilt, AI re-asked | Both scripted and working. |
| A check notices an undocumented screen | Not built. |
| Help menu opens the guide at the installed version | Not built. |
| The AI's reply can point to the page | Not possible today. The chat shows links as plain text. |
| Screen recordings | Not started. |
| Seven pages | One. |

One more limit on the "walk in the app" step: it reuses existing harness runs that happen to exercise the same screens. It proves those screens work as the page says, but it does not check the page sentence by sentence.

**The part I am least sure I have right**

My reading of "repeatable, with minimum human intervention" is that the second row matters most to you: when the code changes, an agent should update the guide's text itself, and a person only approves. Is that what you mean, or do you mean something narrower, such as only the checks and pictures being automatic while a person still writes the pages?
No, I don't want it to be too complicated and fancy. What I need is that the document can be brought in sync with the code before we make another release.

Understood. The goal is one step before each release that brings the guide back in line with the app, and nothing fancier. I will finish it as that: one command that says what is out of date and retakes the pictures, plus a short written step in the release procedure saying to run it and fix what it reports. I am dropping the rest of what I listed.

    An entry with "checks" depends on those named checks alone: the run is
    stopped once they have passed, and a failure elsewhere in it is reported
    apart, since it is not about the page. Without "checks" the whole run
    has to pass. The harness gives up by itself after 900 s."""
    args = [str(out) if arg == "{dir}" else arg for arg in entry["args"]]
    # The harness makes its data folder in the temporary folder: keep it beside the run.
    env = dict(os.environ, TMPDIR=str(out / "data"),
               **{name: str(out) if value == "{dir}" else value for name, value in entry.get("env", {}).items()})
    (out / "data").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    needed = set(entry.get("checks", []))
    passed, failed, lines = set(), [], []
    process = subprocess.Popen([str(binary), *args], env=env, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
                               text=True, errors="replace")
    for line in process.stdout:
        lines.append(line)
        check = re.search(r"HARNESS CHECK (\\S+) (PASS|FAIL)", line)
        if check:
            (passed.add if check.group(2) == "PASS" else failed.append)(check.group(1))
        if needed and (needed <= passed or needed & set(failed)):
            process.terminate()
            break
    process.wait()
    text = "".join(lines)
    log.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")

        return not missing, [f"{name} did not pass" for name in missing], len(passed), [name for name in failed if name not in needed]

# JusPrin guide

How to use JusPrin, one page per part of the app.

- [Seeing and changing print settings](print-settings.md)

## Before a release

The guide is brought in line with the app before each release, on a computer with the app built.

1. Build the app's test harness and pages from the commit to release: the `shell_integration_harness` and `jusprin_web` targets.
2. Leave the computer alone and run `scripts/check_guide.py --ask-ai`. It takes about a minute a page, plus the questions.
3. Fix what it reports, then run it again until it passes:
   - **A label is on no screen.** The app's wording changed. Find the new wording in the app and correct the page.
   - **A run failed.** Open its log, which the command names. Either the screen no longer works as the page says, and the page needs correcting, or the harness expects something the app no longer does, and the harness needs correcting.
   - **A picture is blank.** The program that started the command may not record the screen. Grant it Screen Recording in the system's privacy settings and run again.
   - **AI answered a question wrongly.** Read its reply in the output. Usually the page is unclear or its first line does not say when to read it.
4. Look through what changed on screen since the last release (`git log <last release tag>..HEAD -- src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin`). The command finds what a page gets wrong. It cannot find a new screen or menu item that no page mentions, so add those by hand.
5. Commit the pages together with their pictures and the skills the command rebuilt.

## What the command does

1. **Walks the app and takes the pictures.** `tests/shell/guide_checks.json` names, for each page, the runs of the app's test harness that go through the screens the page describes, and the checks in each run the page depends on. `tests/shell/run_guide_checks.py` runs them in the app as built and copies the pictures a page uses into `pictures/<page>/`.
2. **Rebuilds the copy AI reads.** `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/guide.ts` builds a skill from each page.
3. **Checks each page**, in `guide.test.ts` beside it: every label in bold is in the app's source, every section has a run in step 1, every picture is one step 1 took, and the page has questions for step 4.
4. **Asks AI the page's questions** (`--ask-ai`). `tests/project_prompt/guide_questions.json` holds them with what a right answer says. `tests/project_prompt/run_guide_tests.py` asks the model and has a judge read the replies.

## Writing a page

- Start it with `<!-- ai-description: … -->`: one line, at most 300 bytes, saying when AI should read it.
- Put words that are only for AI in `<!-- ai: … -->`. They are hidden on this site.
- Use bold only for words that are on screen, exactly as they are on screen.
- A picture goes on a line of its own, as `![what it shows](pictures/<page>/<name>.png)`, and comes from a run named in `guide_checks.json`. AI's copy leaves it out.
- Give each `##` section a run in `guide_checks.json`.
- Add at least three questions for the page to `guide_questions.json`.
- AI's copy may hold at most 16 KiB. Split a page that grows past that.

There is now one command that brings the guide in line with the app before a release, and it passed from start to finish on this Mac. The page has its pictures, taken from the built app, and everything is pushed on `claude/app-guide`.

**What you do before a release**

1. Build the app's test harness and pages from the commit you will release.
2. Leave the computer alone and run this. It takes about a minute for the page, plus the questions.

```bash
scripts/check_guide.py --ask-ai
```

3. Fix whatever it reports and run it again until it passes.

The steps are written in [docs/guide/README.md](https://github.com/TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin/blob/claude/app-guide/docs/guide/README.md), under "Before a release". I also added one line to `AGENTS.md` pointing to it. That line is my addition to your rules file, so remove it if you do not want it there.

**What the command does**

- **Checks the page against the running app.** It drives the built app through the screens the page describes, using the test harness the repository already had, and fails if a check fails.
- **Retakes the pictures** from those same runs, and refuses a blank one.
- **Rebuilds the AI's copy** of each page.
- **Checks the page's wording.** It fails if a button name the page quotes is no longer in the app.
- **Asks the AI the page's questions** and has a second model judge the answers.

**What I ran and the result**

- The five harness runs for the print settings page pass, in about 45 seconds together.
- The AI answered 8 of 8 questions from the guide on Sonnet 5.5, one run each.
- All 725 page tests and the prompt suite's 91 unit tests pass.
- The C++ test I could not run earlier now passes: the recorded tool list matches what the app sends.

**See the page**

[print-settings.md on GitHub](https://github.com/TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin/blob/claude/app-guide/docs/guide/print-settings.md) now shows five pictures: the setup summary, the All settings list, one object's own settings, the "Revert to here" question, and the plates panel. The pictures caught one mistake in my text. "Revert to here" is a small arrow button beside a change, not a text button, and the page now says so.

**What still needs a person**

- **A permission, once.** Pictures of whole windows, such as the menus and classic view, came out black, because the program that launches the harness has no screen-recording permission on this Mac. The page has no such pictures yet. You would grant it under Privacy & Security in System Settings, and I cannot do that for you.
- **A quiet computer while it runs.** The harness takes real clicks. A run failed once when another window came to the front, so the command now retries a failed run once.
- **New screens.** The command finds what a page gets wrong. It cannot find a new menu item that no page mentions, so the written steps say to look through what changed since the last release.

**Two things I found on the way**

- The harness was not built anywhere, so I built it in my worktree. That took 28 minutes.
- One harness mode expected old wording on the setup card and waited 15 minutes for it. I corrected those two lines. Two later checks in that mode still fail. They are about the AI applying a change, not about this page, so I left them and the command reports them separately.

**Not done**

Six of the seven pages are unwritten, and the Help menu item that opens the guide is not built.

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.

**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Feed the key from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`jusprin_agent.openai_api_key`) via env without echoing it. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.

- Signed-in conf needs all of: `jusprin_agent.{provider=jusprin, jusprin_api_key, enabled=true, cloud_consent=true, jusprin_model_formats=<JSON id→format from GET /ent/jusprin/v2/models>}`, `jusprin_server.base_url`, `jusprin_onboarding.status=completed`. - `Contents/Resources` in the build is a symlink to the worktree. Replace it with a real folder of links before corrupting a resource, or the worktree gets corrupted.
- Bringing the app forward triggers an account refresh, so to race the gateway (a real 402), change the ledger and send without refocusing.
- Page text input: native value setter plus an `input` event. A modal Preferences window's page polls as `agent-preferences`.
- A test preset needs a `version` field or import rejects it.

On 2026-10-28 I walked six scenarios (open-and-print, fix-a-problem) through the real app with Opus 5.5 and published the critique at https://claude.ai/artifact/XyVvteGiKhiJ6apUx8rcmR (34 frames, scratch copy at scratchpad/ux/ of that session). Kenneth's steer: start from files people actually download (MakerWorld 3MFs carry a full Bambu profile: printer, print preset, filaments, colours, bed type, designer, licence), not from generated STLs. `~/Downloads` has Tape_4_3MF.3mf (A1 mini profile), find_my_hollow.3mf (P1S, 3 colours, 233 mm wide, too big for an A1 mini), arrow_headband.3mf (P1S), general_purpose_hook.STL (bare).

**Recipe that worked**
- `ditto` the built .app out of `build/arm64/src/RelWithDebInfo/` into the scratchpad before launching (another session's ninja can relink it underneath you); the bundle id is already unique (`io.jusprin.JusPrin`), no re-sign needed.
- `ditto` `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2` to a scratch `--datadir`; set `jusprin.fake_printer=true`, `presets.machine` to the saved "Bambu Lab A1 mini 2", write `jusprin/fake_printer.json`, delete `jusprin/mcp.json.lock`.
- **Clear `local_machines`.** Kenneth's conf carries a `local_machines` entry keyed by the empty string (old Moonraker experiment). With the fake Bambu agent on, `init_networking_callbacks`' connect callback calls `DeviceManager::set_selected_machine("")` in a loop ("same lan machine, dev_id =, disconnect and reconnect"), the main window disappears and the log grew 700 MB in two minutes. Clearing the map fixed it. The loop has no guard; see [[fake-bambu-printer-sim]] and [[harness-fake-printer-cleanup]].
- Background `app_*` tools cannot press OrcaSlicer's custom `Button`s (no AX action) and the hit test at the dialog's screen position reports "belongs to a different process". `request_full_control` + `computer_batch` works for everything, including the Agent web view and the macOS file chooser (`cmd+shift+g`, type the path, Return, Return). Re-front the app with `open_application` when another session's harness steals focus.
- Every `app_screenshot`/`computer_batch` screenshot is written as a JPEG under `~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session>/tool-results/mcp-computer-use-blob-*.jpg`; copy those for a report instead of fighting `screencapture`.
- The dev build (-O0) slices a 38 mm part in over a minute; wait 45–60 s before judging a slice.

**Why:** the first launch attempt looked like an app bug (blank window, title "Couldn't save") and cost ten minutes; the dialog-click refusals cost another ten.
**How to apply:** reuse this for any "walk through the app as a user" request; keep scenarios on downloaded files; write the critique per step as what the person knows / sees / finds confusing. Related: [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[drive-app-with-posted-key-events]].

Met while verifying print-host printer window fixes on the scratch `.app` (see [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[open-file-in-app-without-screen-control]]).

- **Copy a new build into a `.app` with `rm` then `cp`.** `cp` over the existing signed binary keeps the inode; the kernel kills the launch at once (exit 137, nothing logged).
- **A launch from a plain Bash call dies when the call ends.** Start the app with `run_in_background: true` and `exec`.
- **Home ignores bridge messages while the main window shows a project.** A queued `launch_monitor` through `JUSPRIN_HOME_DEV_URL` is sent by the page and silently dropped; switch to Home first (`m_tabpanel->SetSelection(0)` via lldb).
- **Background `app_click` does not reach the header's popup menus** (they are not listed as windows). Post the click into the app's queue with lldb: `expr -l objc -- @import AppKit`, then `NSEvent mouseEventWithType:NSEventTypeLeftMouseDown/Up location:NSMakePoint(x, y-from-popup-bottom) ... windowNumber:[popup windowNumber]` and `[NSApp postEvent:atStart:NO]`. Render the popup with `cacheDisplayInRect:` on its contentView ([[capture-mac-popups-for-platform-diff]]).
- **lldb cannot build `std::string` args.** This libc++ uses the alternate short-string layout: a 24-byte char array with the text at offset 0 and its length in byte 23 (≤ 22 chars), passed as `*(std::string*)buf`.
- **wx `wxStaticText::Wrap()` (Orca's wx) skips a width it already wrapped at and keeps the first text it wrapped**, so SetLabel + Wrap on a reused label comes back unwrapped. Use a fresh label.
- **With the screen locked, an instrumented dev page stops polling** (WebKit throttles the hidden page's timers; `document.visibilityState` is "hidden"). Run JS in it through lldb instead: walk `[NSApp windows]` → subviews to the `WKWebView` (match its title or `URL`), then `[webview evaluateJavaScript:@"…" completionHandler:nil]`; the page can `fetch()` results to the dev server. A menu item without a shortcut: `[[item target] performSelector:[item action] withObject:item afterDelay:0.5]` from lldb, so the modal it opens runs after detach.
- **A locked screen slows the whole app 2-4×** (2026-11-05: the same first-launch OrcaSlicer import took 46 s unlocked at 15:48, 226 s locked at 19:22, same build and folder). Compare timings only between back-to-back runs under the same conditions, old and new builds side by side.

The Help menu gains "JusPrin guide…" above Ask AI…. It opens a window over

a proposal Kenneth has not approved.
How it is built:
- The window is the Agent page in a new mode, ?panel=guide
  (AgentPageMode::Guide, Shell/GuideWindow), as Preferences and the import
  windows are. The page carries every docs/guide page and picture, packed in
  when it is built (guidePages.ts), so nothing is installed beside it. That
  took the page from 795 KB to 1.29 MB; WebKit on a Mac opened it in 24 ms

  installing the page's script handler. The guide window hit this first.

Users often ask the in-app AI how to use a feature, and the AI had nothing describing JusPrin's own screens, so it described OrcaSlicer's screens, which JusPrin hides. On 2026-11-11 a guide was started that both people and the AI read, with a process to keep it in line with the app.

The Help window work is done as built, and it is on the branch `claude/guide-window`. The task chip for the remaining guide pages is up and not started.

**Is it done?**

Yes, as far as building goes. I checked it myself instead of relying on the session's report:

- **The commit is on GitHub.** `f63b11d4ee`, "Help › JusPrin guide…: a window that searches the app guide and shows its pages", is the one commit on `claude/guide-window` on top of the guide's branch.
- **Its page tests pass.** I checked that commit out and ran them: 732 tests pass and the type check is clean.
- **I did not rerun its harness runs or open the window myself.** Its commit message says the default harness run has 0 failures and that the window was checked in a built Mac app in light and dark.

**Which branch**

- `claude/guide-window` holds the Help window and everything from `claude/app-guide` under it. This is the one to build on.
- Neither branch is merged into `jusprin-dev`, and no pull request is open.
- `claude/inspiring-aryabhata-8ac5c2` is that session's old branch with the same work as two commits. It left it in place.
- `claude/printer-setup-harness-fixes` is a local, unpushed branch with unfinished fixes to a printer test the session ran into. It wrote a prompt for another session to finish them. That is separate from the guide.

**Two questions that session is still waiting on you for**

- Whether you approve the guide window's design as built.
- Whether the guide's pictures should stay light when the app is in dark mode.

**The new task chip**

"Write the remaining six guide pages" asks a new session to write the six missing pages by the process already built: steps written from the code and checked in the running app, pictures taken from the harness, at least three AI questions a page, and the one command passing for all seven pages. It also asks for the first measurement of whether the AI picks the right guide when several are listed, on your subscription with Sonnet 5.5.

When you set its options, the base branch should be `claude/guide-window`. The card cannot carry that setting, and the pages and the window exist only there.
Now, I hope that you have a clear vision for how we can, what kind of process we will have to make sure the document is up to date after a major update. If so, explain that to me.

Yes. The process is one step done before each release, and it has three parts: a command that finds what is wrong, a person or agent who fixes the pages, and one check that still has to be done by reading.

**An example of how it goes**

Say the next major update renames "All settings" to "Every setting", changes what the plate menu does, and adds a new "Compare plates" item to the View menu. Before the release, someone builds the app from the commit to be released and runs:

```bash
scripts/check_guide.py --ask-ai
```

- **The rename is caught.** The command reports that the print settings page quotes "All settings" and no screen has that label any more.
- **The changed plate menu is caught if a harness check covers it.** The command drives the built app through each page's screens. If the screen no longer behaves as the page says, that run fails and names the check.
- **The pictures are retaken.** A picture that changed shows up in the commit's diff, which tells the reviewer which section to reread.
- **The AI is re-asked each page's questions.** If it stops reading a page or answers wrongly, the command says which question.
- **"Compare plates" is not caught.** No page mentions it, so nothing can be out of date about it. This is the part done by reading: the written steps say to go through what changed on screen since the last release and add what is new.

Whoever runs it fixes the pages, runs the command again until it passes, and commits the pages with their pictures and the AI's copies. That commit is part of the release, so the app ships with a guide that matches it, both for the AI and in the Help window.

**Who does it**

I expect an agent session to do it, started with one sentence such as "bring the guide in line for this release". You review a diff of pages and pictures. The steps are written in `docs/guide/README.md` under "Before a release", and one line in `AGENTS.md` points agents to it.

**What the process does not do, so you can judge it**

- **Nothing forces it to run.** It is a written step someone has to follow. The release workflow already refuses to release without release notes, and a similar refusal for the guide is possible. That is a proposal, and I have not built it because you asked for simple.
- **After a major update, reading for new screens is the biggest part,** and it is manual.
- **It needs a Mac with the app built and left alone,** about a minute a page.
- **The harness it relies on goes stale too.** I found old expectations in it during the first run. The pre-release run surfaces those, and fixing them becomes part of the step.
- **Screens that are stock OrcaSlicer are only pointed to.** After taking a new OrcaSlicer release, changes inside those windows are not covered.

**Where it stands today**

All of this is on the branch `claude/guide-window` and is not merged. It has been run end to end for the one page that exists. The other six pages are being written now in the session you just started, which will be the first real test of the process at full size.

content.text:
The step should be written in the places an agent actually meets while making a release, and today it is not. I looked at how a release is made, and my proposal is three small additions. Nothing is changed yet.

**How an agent learns the release steps today**

There is no written release checklist. The steps live in one place: the comment at the top of the release workflow, `.github/workflows/jusprin_release.yml`. That workflow also teaches by refusing. If the release notes file for the version is missing, it stops with this message: "Write … first. The draft starts with it and the app shows it under What's new." An agent who forgets the notes is told exactly what to do at the moment it matters.

The guide step has nothing like that. I wrote it in `docs/guide/README.md` and in one line under "Documentation" in `AGENTS.md`. An agent doing a release has no reason to open either.

**What I propose**

1. **The release workflow refuses, with a message.** When `scripts/check_guide.py` passes, it would write a one-line record of the app version it was run for. The release workflow would compare that with the version being released. If they differ, it stops and says: run `scripts/check_guide.py --ask-ai` on a built copy of this commit, commit the result, see `docs/guide/README.md`. This is the same pattern as the release notes.
2. **One line in the workflow's top comment,** next to the line about release notes, so the written steps and the refusal agree.
3. **A short "Releasing" section in `AGENTS.md`.** Every agent session loads that file. The section would list what a release needs in one place: the version, the release notes, and the guide check. Today those are scattered, and my one line sits under the wrong heading.

**What this does and does not guarantee**

- An agent cannot start a release for a new version without being told about the guide.
- The record proves someone ran the check for that version. It does not prove they ran it on the final commit, or that they read through what is new on screen. That reading step stays a written instruction.
- The workflow itself cannot run the app, so it cannot do the check on its own. It can only ask for the record.

**Decision needed.** Whether a release can be refused over the guide is yours to decide, because it adds a way for a release to stop. With the refusal, a forgotten guide check blocks the release until someone runs it, which costs a few minutes at a bad moment but cannot be missed. With written steps only, nothing can block a release, but the step depends on an agent reading it, and the first run already showed that unenforced things in this repository go stale. My pick is the refusal, for the same reason the release notes have one. Which do you want?

input.background:
JusPrin is a fork of OrcaSlicer with an in-app AI chat. An app guide was added on 2026-11-11: seven pages in `docs/guide`, each also built into a skill the AI can read (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/skills/guide-<page>/SKILL.md`). Each guide adds one line to the list that the `skill_read` tool's description carries, and that description is sent with every request of the project chat. So the guides change what the model reads on every request, even when nobody asks a how-to question. The system prompt itself was not changed.

The project's rule (and Kenneth's standing instruction) is that any change to what the model reads is not done until the live prompt suite in `tests/project_prompt` has run against the stored baseline. That run has not happened for the guides. The suite's own unit tests pass, and a separate measurement of how-to questions (`tests/project_prompt/run_guide_tests.py`) was run on the Claude subscription with Sonnet 5.5: the session that wrote the pages reports 111 of 111 right. That measurement does not show whether the existing cases got worse, which is what this task is for.

All the guide work is in one line of four commits, pushed to origin and not merged into `jusprin-dev`: `claude/app-guide` (a05657617b), `claude/guide-window` (f63b11d4ee), `claude/guide-pages` (b49541e109), `claude/release-guide-check` (37bbb0e05d, the top, which holds everything). Start from `origin/claude/release-guide-check` at 37bbb0e05d. Note that a local branch named `claude/release-guide-check` in another session's worktree is an older commit, 59a295549f, from before the branches were put in one line; do not use it.

The suite's baseline is `tests/project_prompt/baseline.json`: DeepSeek V4 Flash on the pinned hosts through OpenRouter, judged by gpt-5.5-2026-04-23, recorded 2026-11-03 at 3e662278ea, 22 of today's 24 cases have counts. The keys are in `~/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env`, outside the repository. On 2026-10-10 an earlier session's live tests used more than 300 million tokens and hit the key's monthly limit, so Kenneth's rule is: no live-model run without his approval of a specific batch.

Kenneth's communication rules are in `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` and the project's in `AGENTS.md`: full sentences, no invented labels, proposals marked as proposals, decisions asked in full starting with "Decision needed", outcomes reported with what was tested, under about 500 words.
input.prompt:
Run the project chat's live prompt suite once on the guide branch, compare it with the stored baseline, and tell Kenneth whether the seven guides made any existing case worse. Change no code and commit nothing.

Read first: `tests/project_prompt/README.md`, at least "One step, with its reads answered", "What keeps it faithful to the app", "Running it", and "Judging a prompt or skill change", which is the procedure to follow. Follow it exactly: run the new version only, with the runner's defaults (the checkout, DeepSeek V4 Flash on the pinned hosts, the OpenAI judge, three runs a case, no flags that change the setup), and let the runner print every case beside the baseline.

The batch Kenneth has asked for, by starting this task: one full default run, 24 cases at three runs each, which is 72 runs plus the judge's calls. On 2026-10-15 a comparable 69-run batch used about 1.26 million input tokens, most of them cached. That one run is all that is approved. Before anything more, such as rerunning one case alone at 20 runs, a `--prompt-rev` comparison, another model, or a second full run, stop and ask Kenneth in full with the size of what you want to run. If any request answers `403 Key limit exceeded`, stop and report; do not switch keys or route around it.

How to run:
- Work in your own worktree at `origin/claude/release-guide-check` (37bbb0e05d). The prompt is rendered with node from the AgentUI page, so run `npm ci` in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI` first.
- The runner needs the `tool_call_check` program and refuses one that is older than `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp` in your checkout. A Release build of it from the same source already exists at `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin-worktrees/app-guide/build/arm64/tests/agent/Release/tool_call_check`. You may use it through `JUSPRIN_TOOL_CALL_CHECK` after confirming with `cmp` that your `ToolRegistry.cpp` is byte for byte the same as the one in that folder, and then setting your file's time to match with `touch -r`. Do not build or change anything in that folder. If the files differ, build the `tool_call_check` target in your own build folder instead, following the shared-machine build rules in `AGENTS.md`.
- Run the suite's own unit tests first, which send nothing: `python3 -m unittest test_steps test_prefix_check test_claude_cli` in `tests/project_prompt`. They should report 91 tests passing.
- Then the live run, with the keys loaded in a subshell so they never reach a log: `( . "$HOME/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env"; tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py --results <a file in your scratch folder> )`. Keep the full output in a file. Never print the key file or echo a key.
- Run it in the background and check its progress; do not start a second copy.

What to expect and how to read it:
- The comparison will say that the tool list differs from the baseline's, because of the seven guide lines. That is the change being measured.
- As the README says, at three runs a case only a large move is marked. Read every failed and unobserved run of every case, marked or not, and say for each whether it looks like something the guides caused: for example the model calling `skill_read` on a guide where the case expected a reply or another read, or a run ending unobserved because it read a guide the recording has no answer for. Count how many runs called `skill_read` with a `guide-` name at all.
- Do not record a new baseline. Whether these counts become the baseline is Kenneth's decision.
- The printer chat's suite (`tests/printer_prompt`) should not need running, because the printer chat is not sent the list of guides (`AgentHost.cpp`, where `skill_index` is filled only for a session with no tool list of its own). Confirm that in the code and say so, rather than running it.

Done looks like a report to Kenneth with: the table of every case beside its baseline; what you concluded for each failure and unobserved run; how many runs read a guide and whether that hurt them; the tokens used; anything that could not be judged; and your recommendation on whether the guide branch is safe to merge as far as this suite can show. If the result is unclear, say so and ask the decision in full, with the size and cost of the extra run that would settle it.

content.text:
The two branches are stacked and pushed, the task chip for the live prompt suite is up, and your approval of the Help window is passed on. Your third reply needs a correction from me, which is at the end.

**Stack and push**

All the guide work is now one line of four commits on GitHub:

| Branch | Commit | Holds |
|---|---|---|
| `claude/app-guide` | `a05657617b` | The first page and the pre-release command |
| `claude/guide-window` | `f63b11d4ee` | The Help window with search |
| `claude/guide-pages` | `b49541e109` | The six other pages |
| `claude/release-guide-check` | `37bbb0e05d` | The release refusal and its tick box, on top of everything |

The release check went on top of the pages without a conflict. On the stacked result I ran:

- the page tests: 762 pass, and the type check is clean;
- the release checks: 16 pass;
- the C++ test of the recorded tool list: passes with all seven guides;
- the prompt suite's unit tests: 91 pass;
- the guide command without its app step: passes.

I did not rerun the walk through the built app or the questions to the AI. Those rest on the pages session's report.

Two things to know:

- **The next release will be refused as things stand.** No full guide check has been run since the refusal was added, so the record file it looks for does not exist yet. A full run of the command, or the tick box, clears it.
- **One local branch is now out of date.** The release session's worktree still has `claude/release-guide-check` at its old commit, from before stacking. GitHub has the new one.

Nothing is merged, and `jusprin-dev` is 11 commits ahead of this line's base.

**The live prompt suite chip**

"Run the live prompt suite on the guide branch" is up and not started. Its brief sets the batch at one full default run: 24 cases, three runs each, on DeepSeek V4 Flash with the usual judge. It tells the session to stop and ask you before running anything more. Set its base to `claude/release-guide-check`, which holds everything.

**Your approval**

I passed "approved" to the Help window session. I read it as approving the design as built, including how it shows pictures in dark mode. If you meant something different about the pictures, say so.

**Releases started by pushing a branch**

I was unclear before, and I am sorry for the confusion. What I said was that only the release publisher, you, can run the workflow. That is about who, not how. There are two ways to start it, and the workflow's own comment lists both: the "Run workflow" button on the Actions page, or pushing a branch whose name starts with `jusprin-release/`.

The tick box is on the button's form. A pushed branch has no form, so on that route there is no box to tick. As built, a release started by a push is refused when the guide was not checked, and the only way past it is to run the check.

**Decision needed.** This only matters if you ever start a release by pushing a branch. Keeping it as built means that route always requires the guide check, which is the stricter choice and needs no more work. Letting pushed releases skip the check would make that route a silent way around the refusal, which defeats its purpose. My pick is to keep it as built.

content.text:
Partly. I would squash the first two commits into one and keep the other three as they are. I would not squash everything into a single commit.

First, a correction: I have been saying "four commits". It is five commits on four branches.

| Commit | What it is | Files | App code files |
|---|---|---|---|
| `d23e736c47` | The first page, built into a skill the AI reads | 8 | 0 |
| `a05657617b` | The pre-release command and the pictures | 17 | 0 |
| `f63b11d4ee` | The Help window, and a change to how six windows close their web views | 38 | 21 |
| `b49541e109` | The six other pages | 45 | 0 |
| `37bbb0e05d` | The release refusal | 6 | 0 |

**Why squash the first two**

They are one piece of work, and the second corrects the first. The first commit's message says the page's steps were never checked in the app and that it has no pictures. The second fixes both. Kept apart, the history records a state that was never meant to stand.

**Why keep the others separate**

- **The Help window is the only commit that touches app code,** and it changes how six existing windows release their web views. If that ever causes a crash, you will want to find it and undo it alone, without losing the guide pages.
- **The release refusal is a change to how releases work.** If it gets in the way one day, undoing it should not touch anything else.
- **The six pages are content.** They could fold into the guide commit, but they sit after the Help window and depend on it, so folding them means reordering history for little gain.

That leaves four commits, each of which can be read, reviewed and undone by itself.

**One message to fix on the way**

The Help window commit's message still says its design is a proposal you have not approved. You have approved it since. Rewriting history is the one chance to correct that line.

**When to do it**

During the rebase onto `jusprin-dev`. The line is 11 commits behind and has to be rebased before it can land, which changes every commit's hash anyway. Squashing at the same moment costs nothing extra. Squashing now and rebasing later would rewrite the pushed branches twice.

**What it costs**

All four branches on GitHub get overwritten with new commits. No pull request is open, so nobody reviewing is affected. The four other sessions' worktrees would be left holding the old commits locally.

**Decision needed.** Rewriting pushed history is yours to approve, and you removed the fixed rule about how branches land, so I am not assuming one. Rebasing and squashing the first two gives a clean line of four commits ready to land, at the cost of overwriting four pushed branches. Leaving it as is costs nothing now, but the line stays 11 commits behind and the stale messages stay in the history. My pick is to rebase and squash the first two. Which do you want?

input.content:
App guide: seven pages people and AI read, a Help window, and a release check

The AI in a project chat was told nothing about JusPrin's own screens, so
asked "where do I change the layer height myself?" it described OrcaSlicer's
Prepare sidebar, which JusPrin's view hides. People had no guide either.

The guide. docs/guide holds seven pages, one per part of the app: projects
and files, plates and objects, printers and filament, print settings, slicing
and printing, AI chats and account, and the app itself. Each is written from
the code, quotes on-screen labels in bold, says where menus are on a Mac and
on Windows and Linux, and carries pictures taken from the app as built
(docs/guide/pictures/<page>/).

For AI. AgentUI/src/guide.ts builds a skill from each page
(skills/guide-<page>/SKILL.md, checked in), so skills.ts, the app's tools
test and the wording guard take it as any other skill. A page starts with
<!-- ai-description: … -->, the line skill_read lists it by; <!-- ai: … -->
holds a note only the model gets; pictures are left out of the skill. The
system prompt is unchanged. project_tools.json lists the seven guides as the
app now sends them.

For people. Help › "JusPrin guide…" opens a window that lists the pages in
the order of docs/guide/README.md, searches their sections for the typed
words, and shows a page with its pictures. It is the Agent page in a new
mode, ?panel=guide (Shell/GuideWindow), with every page and picture packed in
when the page is built. Kenneth approved the design as built on 2026-11-11;
it is on the canvas "JusPrin v2", page "JusPrin guide window". Its sizes are
tokens (component.guide), with a guard in test_brand_tokens.cpp.

Web view windows share two pieces of code that six of them each carried.
Agent/WebViewRelease waits before a web view is destroyed while WebKit is
still installing the page's script handler, which crashed the app on macOS
when a window closed right after opening; Home's printer pop-out, the credits
sheet, the Add a printer conversation and the guide window use it.
AgentWebView gains a constructor that owns an in-memory ProjectPersistence,
so the guide, Preferences, Import from OrcaSlicer and the printer
conversation no longer build one beside their view.

Keeping the guide in line with the app. scripts/check_guide.py is the one
command, run before a release (docs/guide/README.md, "Before a release"):

1. tests/shell/run_guide_checks.py runs the shell harness modes that
   guide_checks.json names for each page, in the app as built. A run with
   "checks" is judged by those named checks alone and stopped once they pass.
   A failed run is tried once more, since a run takes real clicks and loses
   them when another window comes to the front. The pictures a page uses are
   cropped from the run's own; a blank one is refused.
2. guide.test.ts rebuilds each skill and fails when a bold label is no longer
   a whole string in the GUI source or the pages, when a section has no
   harness run, when a picture is missing or unused, and when a page has
   fewer than three questions.
3. With --ask-ai, tests/project_prompt/run_guide_tests.py asks the model the
   questions in guide_questions.json and has a judge read the replies;
   --no-guide runs them with the guides off the list.

The release check. When a run of all three steps for every page passes,
check_guide.py writes the app's version to docs/guide/checked-version.txt.
The release workflow's prepare job compares that file with Version.hpp
(release.mjs guide, tested in release.test.mjs) and stops with a message
saying what to run when they differ. "Release without the guide check" on the
Run workflow form lets the run go on with a warning, and the draft's title
then ends in "(guide not checked)". A release started by pushing a
jusprin-release/ branch has no form, so it always needs the file; Kenneth
confirmed that on 2026-11-11. The file records the version the check passed
for, not the commit. It does not exist yet, so the next release is refused
until a full run passes. AGENTS.md gets a Releasing section listing what a
release needs: the version, the release notes and the guide check.

Shell harness changes the pages needed: --preferences-capture, which opens
Preferences, clicks each section and checks the words the pages quote, and
that the guide window lists every page in README order; keys pressed on the
3D view send key down, the character and key up, since the view opens its
tools from the key down after the OrcaSlicer 2.5.0 merge; File menu checks
for New project, Open recent, Export project 3MF and the Import submenu; Mac
snapshots of the header menus and the sliced header, and readback of the 3D
view's pixels. --setup-differences-capture expected the setup card's old
wording and waited 15 minutes for it; it now expects "process with filament."
and "differ". Two later checks of that mode still fail and are not touched:
setup_page_groups_a_printer_setting and setup_differences_agent_applies_the_patch.

Measured, before this commit was squashed from five and moved onto today's
jusprin-dev (519189a293 was its base then):
- How-to questions about print settings, Sonnet 5.5 as model and judge, three
  runs each: with the guide listed 24 of 24 read it and named the right
  place; with it off the list, 3 of 24. DeepSeek V4 Flash, one run each with
  the guide: 8 of 8.
- All seven pages, as the session that wrote the six later ones reports: every
  harness run passes and Sonnet answered 111 of 111 questions.
- The live prompt suite, once, 27 cases at three runs on DeepSeek V4 Flash,
  as the session that ran it reports: no case got worse because of the guides
  and no run read a guide; one case, the step after a settings change is
  applied, went from 3 of 3 to 1 of 3, which it reads as unrelated.
- The guide window, as the session that built it reports: checked in a built
  Mac app in light and dark; the default harness run has 0 failures.

Not checked: Windows and Linux; the release workflow on GitHub, which only
the release publisher can run; whole-window pictures of the first page, which
came out black for want of the Screen Recording grant.
